history.summary: Each internal_tls consumer now declares its leaf in one importable task file — proxmox_host's extracted from main.yml, microk8s's carrying the eligibility gate and the install stat it reads (tasks/check-installed.yml) so the gate is right on both entry paths, openbao's already standalone. The two reloads carry their own blast-radius limit: Restart microk8s kubelite is a single throttle-1 task that restarts and then waits for this node's own kubelite endpoint (16443/livez on an apiserver node, kubelet healthz on a worker), and Reload openbao is throttle 1 so the Raft peers never SIGHUP together; throttle rather than serial, verified locally that it serializes strictly and that a failing host does not stop the others. Gate green (yamllint + ansible-lint).
ansible: cexec iac poetry run ansible-lint    [  OK  ]

Both P1 outcomes land and I verified the load-bearing mechanisms independently: the standalone `tasks_from: internal_tls` entry works with the hoisted gate, and throttle-on-a-handler serializes strictly while still letting a failed host's peers run and still exiting non-zero. Converge behaviour and the drift signal are unchanged. Three advisory findings, none blocking: check-mode no longer surfaces the kubelite restart, /livez is a weaker signal than the comment's 'serving again', and Restart openbao is left outside the limit its sibling reload now carries.

findings.summary: The kubelite restart handler is a shell task, so a --check --diff run skips it and (with display_skipped_hosts=False) never names the control-plane bounce an apply will do.
The wait gates on /livez (and kubelet healthz on a worker), which omit etcd-readiness/informer-sync — weaker than the 'only once this one is serving' the handler comment claims.
Reload openbao gained throttle: 1 but the more disruptive Restart openbao in the same role still relies on the caller's serial.

history.summary: ansible/playbooks/renew-internal-tls.yml renews all ten internal_tls leaves in one play over proxmox:k8s:openbao, entering each consumer role at its own internal_tls task file so nothing about a leaf is restated; srvk8s4 drops out through the microk8s gate. One play rather than one per group because Ansible abandons the whole run when every host of a play fails (proved locally, and max_fail_percentage does not lift it); no serial, so the one-at-a-time guarantee stays with P1's throttled handlers; force_handlers so a host failing after issuance cannot drop its pending reload. Gate green, done-record appended, P3 gained the handler-phase timing constraint.
ansible: cexec iac poetry run ansible-lint    [  OK  ]

renew-internal-tls.yml meets P2's outcome: one play over proxmox:k8s:openbao reaches all ten leaves through P1's declarations with nothing restated, resolves to the predicted 11 hosts and cuts cleanly into P3's two scopes. I reproduced the two load-bearing mechanisms against the pinned ansible-core — cross-role handler resolution under a conditional import_role, and force_handlers rescuing a pending reload on a host that fails after issuance while its peers complete and the run still exits non-zero. One advisory finding: a comment misattributes why serial: costs fleet coverage.

findings.summary: The no-serial comment (renew-internal-tls.yml:64-71) claims serial: defaults max_fail_percentage to 0; it has no default and the linear strategy skips it unless set — the real break is the batch-fully-failed check in playbook_executor.py:190-195, so the remedy the comment implies does not work.

history.summary: Jenkinsfile.iac-scheduled-certs now renews the internal_tls leaves in the same job and Friday slot as the SSH host certs: four stages (host certs prd/dev, then TLS leaves prd/dev), prd untimed and reddening the build, dev probed with devUp() and only ever UNSTABLE (page only on a genuine failure). The shared post block was made truthful for two classes — each prd stage writes its own failure description via a stage-level post block, and both dev stages feed the existing DEV_STAGE_FAILED page gate. kc project test is green; no Groovy parser exists here, so the pipeline syntax is reviewed, not machine-checked.

P3's outcome holds: iac-scheduled-certs runs the leaf renewal on the same Friday cron and the same two scopes as the host certs, the host-cert stages are renamed only and still run first, and the split build descriptions are truthful in both directions. Two advisory findings, neither blocking: the dev page is lost when a dev stage's flag is followed by a prd stage failure, and the catch-all failure description is gone. The largest residual risk — a red host-cert stage aborting before either leaf stage — is already recorded as close-out S4 and not re-filed.

findings.summary: notify.warning fires only from post { unstable }, so a dev stage's DEV_STAGE_FAILED page is lost once a later prd stage reds the build — newly reachable because P3 puts prd work after a dev stage.
Removing the job-level post { failure } leaves a red build with no description at all when the failure is outside the two prd stages (library step, agent allocation, SCM checkout).

history.summary: decisions.md's "Cluster changes are serialized" principle (:26) now states the invariant — never two k8s or Ceph nodes mutated at once — with serial: 1 as one mechanism for it, the coverage cost it carries (first failed or unreachable host ends the play, rest untried; max_fail_percentage does not lift it, verified by local probe against the repo's own ansible), and the alternative this slice ships: throttle: 1 on the mutating task with the readiness wait inside it. The RBAC entry (:294) no longer attributes its one-node-at-a-time roll to site-k8s.yml's serial: 1. No other serialization claim in decisions.md is falsified by the shipped diff; done-record appended and committed on phase/016-P4.

P4's outcome holds: decisions.md:26 now states the serialization invariant with `serial: 1` as one mechanism rather than the rule, and :294 no longer misattributes the RBAC roll to site-k8s.yml's serial. I verified the load-bearing new claim two ways — reading the pinned ansible-core 2.20.5 (the entire-batch-failed break is unconditional) and running the probe (serial: 1 with max_fail_percentage: 100, first host failing, ends the play at that host, exit 2) — and confirmed no other serialization claim in decisions.md is falsified. Two advisory prose imprecisions in the rewritten sentence, neither blocking.

findings.summary: decisions.md:26 credits both throttled handlers with an in-task readiness wait, but Reload openbao (roles/openbao/handlers/main.yml:13-23) is a bare systemd reload with throttle: 1 and no wait.

decisions.md:26 states 'never two k8s or Ceph nodes mutated at once' unqualified, while renew-internal-tls.yml — endorsed four clauses later — installs new leaves on srvk8s1/2/3 concurrently; only the restart is serialized.

history.summary: Every requirement and ruling in the plan is delivered by a merged phase and I can point at the implementing work for all nineteen acceptance criteria: R1 by renew-internal-tls.yml (P2) plus the two new stages in Jenkinsfile.iac-scheduled-certs (P3), the coverage ruling by the one play over proxmox:k8s:openbao with srvk8s4 dropping out through the microk8s gate P1 hoisted, the serialize-without-losing-coverage ruling by throttle: 1 with an in-task readiness wait on Restart microk8s kubelite and throttle: 1 on Reload openbao (P1) plus force_handlers and no serial: on the play (P2), the single-declaration ruling by the three per-consumer internal_tls task files (P1), the stalled-renewer ruling by the job's own red-or-unstable signal with no Prometheus claim anywhere (P3), and the doctrine ruling by decisions.md:26 and :294 (P4). No done-record admits a leftover that the loop's own later stages do not own: the three doc leftovers P1/P2/P4 named (proxmox_host/README.md:55, playbooks/README.md, decisions.md:140's 'has no scheduled driver', which this slice falsifies) are diff-based reconciliation on surfaces 1 and 3 of docs/slice-doc-plan.md, which is the doc phase's job and not a phase of the plan. Everything else outstanding is already close-out material at close-out weight - nine bugs and four suggestions, none of which the plan owes. I fixed three prose inaccuracies as mechanical residue rather than reporting them: the no-serial comment in renew-internal-tls.yml blamed max_fail_percentage (Ansible b7de205), and decisions.md:26 credited both throttled handlers with a readiness wait and stated the never-two-nodes invariant in a form the endorsed playbook contradicts (AnsibleSpecs c4c048c); kc project lint, build and test are green on the fixed tree and B5, B8 and B9 are struck.

Ran the full slice-testing-strategy procedure: gates taken as established GREEN per dispatch, diff read in full across all four phases (Jenkins + AnsibleSpecs), and live read-only verification against the real prd fleet -- host resolution, srvk8s4's skip, and idempotence all confirmed live, plus direct cert reads showing pve/pve1/pve2 and srvk8s1/2/3 are genuinely inside their 14-day renewal window right now. Pushed b7de205 to main (pre-authorized under the devlock hold). All 19 verification.json items settled: 18 verified, V01 (the leaves actually get signed by the job) marked owed to operator since a real apply against prd stays operator-gated -- operator command is in V01 and close-out N1. No finding cleared the generation bar; two close-out notes added (N1: six leaves due now, with the command; N2: iac-on-push's result for b7de205 unconfirmed this pass, jenkins MCP was down).

Updated every surface that described the leaves as having no scheduled renewer or as renewed by the --check-only drift cycle: the internal_tls, proxmox_host, openbao, microk8s and ssh_host_cert role READMEs, the playbook catalogue, the OpenBao and ssh-host-cert-expiry runbooks, step-ca-bootstrap's two unworkable 'run the drift cycle' instructions, support/iac-agent's job inventory, the slice-testing-strategy serial check, and three bullets in AnsibleSpecs decisions.md (:65, :256, :458 — :26 and :294 were already settled by P4). kc project lint and kc project test both green; committed as 658a341 (Ansible, phase/016-docs) and d736f98 (AnsibleSpecs, main), nothing pushed. No architecture-model nudge: no new host, daemon or external identity, and the model names none of these Jenkins jobs. Close-out carries the doc phase's Summary and Focus lines, B10 (no X.509 counterpart to ssh-host-cert-expiry.md — not written because whether internal_tls re-issues an already-expired leaf could not be grounded from the repo), S5, and notes on B2/B4.
